content.comment_body: Hello. I've built a setup to use cursor keys for cycling pages and illuminating the screen for 15 seconds after any key press. It works in theory, but not on the actual device. The amber light turns on only for the first 15 seconds, and only the first page appears. Could someone advise?

Hello [user_name], your program seems incomplete. What are the purposes of building blocks B003 and B041? It looks like the failure delay remains high, but this can only be verified by checking the original program in online mode. Regards, [user_name]
The main issue is that pressing ESC + Cursor Up does not activate any message. If there's no active message, pressing ESC is interpreted as opening the system menu.

I'll add more details. The more I test, the more issues I encounter. For example, failure text b075 shows up (currently high), but b096 does not—possibly due to priority? You have to go to the clock screen and press ESC to access the menu, but starting on b057 should not affect this. Even if 'Up' is resolved, there are other directions to consider. Also, I've added something at the bottom: the program expects I4 to be off for b058 to energize the relay, but in testing, I had to set I4 high (applying 24VDC from the transformer) for the relay to work. Does anyone need more info? Can someone suggest a solution?

Unfortunately, I can only comment based on your program excerpt. This excerpt cannot be run in [product_name] because the digital output of the shift register is unconnected. Also, when [product_name] is first powered on, no message is active—only the startup screen with the date and time. If the startup screen is showing (no message active) and the ESC key is pressed (with or without cursor key), the device jumps to the system menu.
How can I share a video from my phone with you?
Here is an example for working with the shift register.

[url] I don't understand why the first page displays, nor why the simulation works differently. In the video, I'm manipulating I4 and performing a reset. I want the data logger to record the average value, but it only logs zero—even when logging a calculation from a math instruction, it's still zero.

@[user_name]: It's best to forget using the shift register and cursor keys for this functionality. The keys do not work as the simulation suggests; the actual device behaves differently. As mentioned earlier, the built-in keys only activate under certain screens. You can enable multiple message blocks and scroll with the up/down keys. Use the 'priority' setting in the message block to determine which appears first.
So, the solution is to add another input. I'll try that. Can you guide me specifically on how to log the average value data?

You started discussing the "red car" but shifted to the "blue train"; this makes the topic hard to follow for others. Please keep discussions focused on one main subject. For new issues, begin a new topic in the [product_name] - Software forum and clearly state your goal. Volunteers can only help with the information you provide.

Yes, this conversation has drifted. I realize I need to make some changes to my system to achieve this. One important lesson is that cursor keys shouldn't be used as inputs. Thank you, and please close this discussion.
That's not correct! You do need to know how to use them properly.

The answer is that cursor keys can't be used for these kinds of tasks in your program. They're only intended for maintenance. To use the shift register for rotating message texts and linking it to display amber, you need to dedicate an additional input.

That's not entirely true. Cursor keys can also be used for program control, but the operator then needs to press the ESC key. Based on my experience, it's not very practical and should be used sparingly.
No, that's incorrect. As I've already mentioned in my other reply, that's not right! You just need to know how to use them.

analysis.insight_summary: Users tried to set up cursor keys on a [company_name] [product_name] to cycle through pages and activate the amber backlight, but the hardware did not match simulation behavior. Issues arose with message display, shift register connections, and input logic. Ambiguities and lack of clear documentation, along with inconsistent data logging, led to confusion about program flow and message prioritization.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the cursor keys to consistently switch between multiple pages and trigger the screen backlight every time a key is pressed, similar to simulation results. They also expect accurate average value logging to match what is seen during simulation.
